payload.question: which detections can be decommissioned or retuned without losing true-positive coverage?

evidence.note: No supporting evidence found for failed-login-burst detection value or noise cost. T1110 fetch returned only mitigation text and a report title, no analytic addressing burst thresholds.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK detection guidance for T1059.001 describes behavioral-chain analytics (encoded commands, unusual parent, follow-on activity) rather than alerting on any PowerShell execution.

citations.quote: Detects behavioral chains where PowerShell is launched with encoded commands, unusual parent processes, or suspicious modules loaded, potentially followed by network connections or child process spawning.

evidence.note: Supports retune toward behavioral conditions only. No evidence found on actual alert-noise volume of the any-execution rule.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK analytics for T1071.004 key on query volume, subdomain length and encoding, not TLD rarity.

citations.quote: Detects clients issuing DNS queries with high volume, long subdomain lengths, encoded payload patterns, or to known malicious infrastructure; indicative of DNS-based C2 channels.

evidence.note: No supporting evidence found that rare-TLD queries specifically give true-positive coverage; only the narrow claim above is supported.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK analytic for T1053.005 pairs task creation/modification with subsequent execution via svchost.exe or taskeng.exe.

citations.quote: Detects the creation, modification, or deletion of scheduled tasks through Task Scheduler, WMI, PowerShell, or API-based methods followed by execution from svchost.exe or taskeng.exe.

evidence.note: Supports that creation-only alerting is narrower than published guidance. No noise-rate evidence found.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK detection strategy for T1204.002 is framed as a file open to spawn chain.

citations.quote: Detection Strategy ID Name Analytic ID Analytic Description DET0294 User Execution – Malicious File via download/open → spawn chain (T1204.002) AN0819 User opens a file delivered by email, web, chat, or share.

evidence.note: Supports that this detection type has published coverage value. No evidence on noise or on which parent/child pairs to exclude.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK analytic for T1571 targets processes making outbound connections on uncommon ports or protocol/port mismatch.

citations.quote: Processes initiating outbound connections on uncommon ports or using protocols inconsistent with the assigned port.

evidence.note: Supports process-context and protocol-mismatch conditions as retune direction. No noise-rate evidence found.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK analytic for T1047 describes a multi-event chain (process creation, command execution, network connection if remote).

citations.quote: Detects adversarial abuse of WMI to execute local or remote commands via WMIC, PowerShell, or COM API through a multi-event chain: process creation, command execution, and corresponding network connection if remote.

evidence.note: Supports unique remote-execution coverage value. No noise-rate evidence found.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK analytic for T1547.001 correlates Run-key modification with new or unusual binary paths or script payloads.

citations.quote: Correlation of Registry key creation/modification events under known Run/Startup keys with new or unusual binary paths or script-based payloads.

evidence.note: Supports retune by adding binary-path conditions, not decommission. No noise-rate evidence found.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK analytic for T1055 relies on memory-manipulation API calls and remote thread creation, not rare parent-child process pairs.

citations.quote: Detects process injection by correlating memory manipulation API calls (e.g., VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory), suspicious thread creation (e.g., CreateRemoteThread), and unusual DLL loads within another process's context.

evidence.note: Supports only that rare parent-child is not the published injection signal. No evidence found that the rare-pair rule is redundant with injection telemetry.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK analytic for T1102 keys on uncommon processes making HTTPS connections to web services, not on proxy URL category.

citations.quote: Detects unusual outbound connections to web services from uncommon processes using SSL/TLS, particularly those exhibiting high outbound data volume or persistence.

evidence.note: No supporting evidence found that uncategorized-proxy-category alerts yield true positives.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK guidance for T1567.002 describes chained sensitive-read plus external-upload analytics, matching the egress logic of this rule.

citations.quote: Defender perspective: detect sensitive file reads by non-standard applications followed by unusual encrypted uploads to external cloud storage domains.

claims.claim: Published ATT&CK guidance for T1052.001 describes USB insertion followed by high-volume or sensitive file access.

citations.quote: Detects USB device insertion followed by high-volume or sensitive file access and staging activity by suspicious processes or accounts.

evidence.note: No supporting evidence found for the departing-user (resignation/termination) trigger: SEI and CISA fetches returned only generic passages with no departing-employee or exfiltration monitoring text. T1213.003 and T1048 have analytics (bulk repository download; unusual outbound transfer) but none cited. Retention of this rule on coverage grounds rests only on the claims above.

payload.uncertainty: Google SRE page fetched but its passages (generic alert definitions) do not directly address noise-vs-signal tradeoffs for any candidate, so it is cited nowhere. No evidence on actual alert volumes or true-positive rates for any detection; ATT&CK pages show published analytics only, not that these specific rules overlap or are redundant.

payload.summary: No verdict is final; every non-keep item needs human approval. D002, D016, D018 decommissions held in 20/20 seeds, so at best approve_with_human_review (synthetic, modelled magnitudes). D005 and D031 retunes to t40 lost no scenario in any seed and are approve_with_human_review with a rollback to the old threshold. D031 is weakly supported: the tp=0 vs 48 TP discrepancy is unreconciled, the 48 is derived, and the gain is small. D025 stays keep. D001, D003, D004, D006, D017 stay investigate with no change authorised. Nothing blocked, because no decommission lost coverage in any seed. D013, D019-D024, D026-D030 were not experimented and the D007-D012, D014 keeps are unchanged; they are outside this review.
payload.uncertainty: All data synthetic. No noise-rate data for any rule. No threshold sweeps supplied, so cliff proximity is not assessed for D005 and D031. D031 baseline vs replay TP counts unreconciled; the 48 TP figure is derived. Monitoring window N and rollback triggers need human setting.
